title: Goryeo potters develop sanggam inlay
summary: Goryeo potters developed a distinctive celadon aesthetic, including sanggam decoration made by inlaying carved designs with contrasting slips beneath the glaze.

citations.locator: Mid-twelfth-century production at Buan and Gangjin; sanggam inlay technique
citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: Goryeo potters developed a distinctive celadon aesthetic, including sanggam decoration made by inlaying carved designs with contrasting slips beneath the glaze.
The source places the consolidation of this aesthetic in the mid-twelfth century; 1150 is an approximate display anchor, not an invention year.
Production at Buan and Gangjin combined knowledge adapted from Chinese ceramics with local experimentation. Inlay provided an alternative to painted or incised surface decoration.

review.corroboration: The Met essay’s mid-twelfth-century and inlay passages were inspected together. Independent priority or invention claims were not established and are not made.
